correctness.rationale: For every d>=2, exponent e_d is computed from the defining product. If gcd(d,k)>1, first progression dominates 2 floor(n/d) and second includes the terminal when needed. If gcd(d,k)=1, residue counting yields e_d=-1 exactly for d>1 dividing n and j; otherwise e_d>=0. For d=1, e_1=0. Thus exact denominator product over coprime divisors equals [u]_q. No omitted boundary cases; 4500 grid checks and 20 rational evaluations corroborate.

equivalent_formulations.reasoning: The first proposed iff requires divisibility by every prime power in gcd(n,j); the new iff requires only the prime support of the gcd to divide k. value.rationale: The theorem corrects an explicitly published proposed iff polynomiality criterion for a natural q-central binomial product and determines the full reduced denominator, not just a single counterexample. The infinite prime-power exception shows the distinction between prime support and full gcd valuations is structurally necessary; this directly answers the motivating integrality problem.
